summary: Independent content review of the 200-item classic 9x9 Sudoku batch (art-content-sudoku-4b8e51f4ce2e). All conclusions are derived from the deterministic code verification interface, not from generator summary or inspection. On-disk SHA-256 recomputed and matches the manifest hash exactly (no integrity fail). Enumeration matches the content plan and project.yaml content_plan.target_content_count (200 = seed indices main-easy/001-200 = answer-key entries 1-200). Re-running ph_cli.py verify --type sudoku returned decision PASS, verifiable=true, 200/200 items passed, 0 failed items, confirming solvability, single-solution uniqueness, answer-key correctness, and measured difficulty within the easy tier per the per-item validate() re-derivation. The plan is a single-tier flat easy plan; per rule 05-puzzle-content.md a uniform/flat givens count is correct-by-design and NO difficulty-progression finding is raised. Zero blocker/major findings. Two note-level findings record genuine deferred layout-stage open questions (OQ-1 trim revision, OQ-2 adult-general cell/type-size literal) that are out of scope for content verification and do not affect content correctness.
limitations: Uniqueness, solvability, answer-key correctness, and difficulty-label accuracy are asserted solely on the strength of the code verification interface (ph_cli.py verify), which reports verifiable=true and 200/200 PASS for the sudoku content type; this review does not substitute manual inspection for that code result.
Cell/type size legibility at the target trim and puzzles-per-page density are layout-stage concerns (OQ-2) not evaluable from the content batch alone; they are deferred, not verified here.

findings.location: content/puzzles/sudoku-batch.json (grid rendering) / content-plan.md section 4 and OQ-2
findings.observation: The content plan records (OQ-2) that age_bands.json:adult-general enumerates no per-cell numeric size range for adult puzzle grids and no human-approved cell/type-size literal exists; final cell size and puzzles-per-page are deferred to the design-policy/layout stage.
findings.evidence: content-plan.md section 4 'Cell/type-size numeric literals' and section 11 OQ-2; age_bands.json adult-general band has no cell/type numeric range (only senior-large-print does). This is a layout dependency, not a content-batch defect; code verification (verifiable=true, 200/200 PASS) confirms puzzle correctness independent of rendered cell size.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the adult-general cell/type-size literal and puzzles-per-page density at LAYOUT_AND_FORMAT_BUILD; carry OQ-2 forward to the layout engineer and the accessibility audit. No content regeneration required.
findings.acceptance_test: At layout/build, confirm a recorded cell/type-size value for adult-general 8.5x11 grids that preserves high-contrast legibility (CLAUDE.md section 9) and passes the accessibility audit.

findings.location: project.yaml production.design.trim_size / content-plan.md section 7 and OQ-1
findings.observation: The engine-authoritative trim 8.5x11 is committed, but a revision to the candidate 6x9 trim remains an open human decision (OQ-1) that would materially change page-budget arithmetic; it does not affect the correctness of the 200 verified puzzles.
findings.evidence: content-plan.md section 7 and OQ-1; project.yaml production.design.trim_size='8.5x11' with candidate set ['8.5x11','6x9','7x10']. Content verification is trim-independent; the 200 items pass regardless of final trim.
findings.recommendation: Treat OQ-1 as a layout/human trim decision; no content change is implied. Record whichever trim is chosen at the layout stage and re-derive the page budget there.
findings.acceptance_test: At layout/build, confirm the committed trim value is present in publishing_house.print_pdf.TRIM_SIZES and the page budget is re-derived against the chosen trim.
